stages.title: Verified foundations (real-project-led)
stages.desc: Verification, privacy and safe client publishing first, then the content and design contracts the real site needs. Each task fits in 1–3 sessions of about 2–3 hours.
stages.milestone: MV: every launch verified (marker, health checks). MC: content contract v2 and safe publishing. MD: Design Engine necessities done.

stages.title: Nocturne Foundation app (local first, hosted later)
stages.where: nocturne-foundation repo (created in Phase 3, with approval)
stages.desc: Proven provisioning first (scripted, verified, resumable), then one Next.js app that runs it from the browser on your machine. Hosting comes later, when there is a reason.
stages.milestone: MF1: two verified scripted launches with failure injection. MN: Foundation app version 0 sets up a site end to end.

tasks.t: Verification marker in the site shell
tasks.what: An agency-only siteIdentity.verificationMarker rendered as <meta name="nocturne:marker"> on every page, seeded by the wizard and checked by launch:check --expect-marker.
tasks.why: "Deployed" is not proof that CMS content renders; a unique marker proves CMS → query → render on real HTTP.

tasks.t: JSON-LD visible-content and @id tests
tasks.what: Tests that every JSON-LD string appears in visible page text, @ids are unique across the sitemap, and every WebPage links #website and #organization.
tasks.why: Structured data must describe visible content; today nothing proves it.

tasks.t: Daily health workflow (launch check and dataset privacy)
tasks.what: A scheduled health.yml runs launch:check --json and check:dataset against production daily and opens or updates a GitHub issue on failure, including enquiry storage on a public dataset.
tasks.why: A plan downgrade makes private datasets public; nothing would notice today.

tasks.t: Field classification registry (client-editable allowlist)
tasks.what: One registry of client-editable fields per document and section type, used by client-mode hiding, the agency publish review and any future publish gate, with a CI test that fails when a field is unclassified.
tasks.why: Agency-only marking is a UI denylist today; a new field would be client-editable by default.

tasks.t: Agency publish review for Contributor drafts
tasks.what: Agency Publish lists protected-field changes since the last publish with their authors and asks for confirmation; an agency-only "Waiting for review" list; Contributors see that their changes go to Currawong.
tasks.why: Clients become Contributors (Sanity blocks their publishing); agency publishing must not leak protected changes and review must be easy.

tasks.t: Content contract v2 design note
tasks.what: A short decision note: service and location entities, relationships, JSON-LD mapping, page templates, profile flags and a migration plan.
tasks.why: The full site's content should go in on the final model, not be migrated later.

tasks.t: Content contract v2: services
tasks.what: A service document type with page template, relationships to team members and FAQs, Service JSON-LD from visible fields, fixtures and tests, behind a profile flag.
tasks.why: Services are core to most client businesses and to truthful structured data.

tasks.t: Content contract v2: locations and relationships
tasks.what: A location document type (branches or service areas) related to services and team members, LocalBusiness branch JSON-LD with stable @ids, fixtures and tests.
tasks.why: Multi-location businesses and area-served data need first-class entities.

tasks.t: Section contract v2: split family
tasks.what: The split section gains supportingMedia (for example a video below the image), named looks, consistent actions and a glass legibility rule, with a dry-run migration and visual tests.
tasks.why: Adding a button or video to an existing layout should not need code.

tasks.t: Section contract v2: hero family
tasks.what: The hero adopts the same looks and slot conventions as the split family, keeping its presets and supporting slot.
tasks.why: One grammar across families keeps the Design Engine learnable.

tasks.t: Theme-adaptation contract test
tasks.what: A test that a global Brand colours change updates every section and keeps text contrast of at least 4.5:1 on every surface, glass included.
tasks.why: Global colour changes must adapt dependent sections intelligently.

tasks.t: SEO checks: internal links and orphan pages
tasks.what: launch:check crawls the sitemap and reports orphan pages, broken internal links and services no page links to.
tasks.why: Search-friendly structure needs deterministic checks.

tasks.t: Spike: publish gate security verification
tasks.what: On a scratch Sanity project with no real data: probe what a Contributor-role robot can do by API, Actions API publish with revision guards, History API authors and Access API role reads, and a prototype Contributor Publish action.
tasks.why: The self-service gate must be proven safe before it is built.

tasks.t: Publish gate: server policy and route
tasks.what: A pure policy (allowlist from task 205) and POST /api/publish that checks authors and their current roles, publishes the exact validated revision through the Actions API with both revision guards, rate-limits and audit-logs.
tasks.why: Lets clients publish allowed changes themselves without trusting the Studio UI.

tasks.t: Publish gate: Studio action and experience
tasks.what: A Contributor Publish action calling the route, clear refusal reasons ("Sent to Currawong for review"), README role tables and end-to-end tests.
tasks.why: Client publishing should feel normal while staying enforced.

tasks.t: Setup and deployment runbook from the real launch
tasks.what: A runbook from new project to verified preview and launch, written from the real launch and its timings.
tasks.why: A repeatable, documented process is a 90-day success criterion.

tasks.t: Foundation repo and scripted launch to a verified preview
tasks.what: Create nocturne-foundation (with approval) and script: empty repo plus template history to a pinned tag plus a configuration commit, Vercel project and environment before the push, wait by commit, verify with the marker.
tasks.why: Setup is manual and error-prone; prove repeatable provisioning first. Absorbs task 42.

tasks.t: Provisioning hardening: Sanity authorisation, failure injection, resume
tasks.what: Test Sanity organisation-robot provisioning (or keep the CLI session), inject failures after every create step and prove resume makes no duplicates or orphaned tokens.
tasks.why: Partial failures must never leave billed or unsafe resources.

tasks.t: blueprint.json from the release script
tasks.what: scripts/release.mjs writes blueprint.json (tag, commit, required environment, seed profiles, checks); check:version validates it.
tasks.why: Foundation needs a machine-readable, versioned blueprint.

tasks.t: Foundation app version 0: core
tasks.what: A local Next.js 16 app with a Neon Postgres ledger (Drizzle; org_id and actor on every row), an in-process step runner with resume, the provider modules and verifier from tasks 199 and 211.
tasks.why: Browser-first Foundation without hosted operations yet.

tasks.t: Foundation: projects list and import of existing sites
tasks.what: Projects screen listing every site with links and versions, importing the client register (task 63).
tasks.why: One place to see every project.

tasks.t: Foundation: new-site wizard and run timeline
tasks.what: A five-field wizard (Vercel) and a live run timeline with blocked reasons, resume and undo of resources this run created.
tasks.why: Fast, verified setup from the browser.

tasks.t: Foundation: verification and health views
tasks.what: Per-project verification results and health checks (the same functions as launch:check and health.yml), with a Run checks button.
tasks.why: See problems before clients do.

tasks.t: Search Console import and URL mapping
tasks.what: A service-account import of 28-day windows (final data, paged to 25,000 rows, truncation flagged) and mapping of URLs to Sanity documents, listing unmatched URLs.
tasks.why: Recommendations need real search data tied to documents. Absorbs task 52 with task 210.

tasks.t: Search Health: opportunity cards and change history
tasks.what: Deterministic opportunity cards with evidence and caveats, opening Studio drafts, and before-and-after tracking by document revision. No scores, no automatic publishing.
tasks.why: Evidence-based SEO improvements without invented scores.

tasks.t: Site recipes: seed profiles per business type
tasks.what: Seed profiles that create a whole site structure (pages, sections, content types, navigation) for a business type, built on content contract v2.
tasks.why: Stop recreating architecture and content models per project.

tasks.t: Cloudflare experiment (C-1 to C-4)
tasks.what: Patch for OpenNext #1400 via patch-package or upstream fix, cache bindings so pages render, next/og, Studio and proxy checks, then one approved Workers Paid scratch deploy running the verification suite.
tasks.why: Cloudflare is a long-term hosting choice; prove it before supporting it.

tasks.t: Mobile proof: Expo Android internal APK (with a use case)
tasks.what: An Expo SDK 58 starter builds an Android internal APK on the free plan, installed on an emulator and a phone showing the content marker.
tasks.why: Mobile stays architecture-ready; prove the first step only when there is a use case.
